plan: In a second-price sealed bid auction with independent values, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Since my value is $27, bidding exactly $27 ensures I maximize potential profit. I'll avoid dominated strategies like bidding less (which risks losing unnecessarily) or bidding much higher (which risks paying more than my value). With no prior round history, a true-value bid is most rational given the uncertainty of other bidders' valuations.

With a private value of $31, my goal is to maximize potential profit. Since this is a second-price auction, I want to bid strategically. A pure strategy would be to bid close to my true value but not exactly at it. I'll bid slightly above my midpoint at $35 to signal confidence while leaving room for potential profit. This approach balances aggression with risk management, potentially outbidding competitors while avoiding overpaying.

My private value is $20. In a second-price sealed bid auction, optimal strategy is to bid my true value. If I bid less, I risk losing the item even when winning would be profitable. If I bid more, I might pay more than the item is worth to me. Since values are independently drawn and this is a single round, I'll bid exactly my private value of $20, which maximizes my expected profit.
